headline: The return of facilities used by US forces at Gwangju Military Airport in South Korea is seen as the biggest variable for SK Hynix's planned chip factories on the site, THE ELEC reports.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: the visit and Chey's remarks date from 9 Oct 2026 and the US-base question was raised in parliament on 6 Oct; the 11 and 12 Oct reports add the schedule risk but no new event.
importance_line: If the handover of US-used areas slips, new memory-chip capacity that AI computing and device makers need could arrive later, but no date is set and South Korea's foreign minister told parliament the US was unlikely to refuse.
summary: THE ELEC reports that SK Group chairman Chey Tae-won toured the Gwangju Military Airport site on 9 Oct 2026 and promised to build as fast as possible, but that the return of areas used by US forces, which must come back before factories can be built, is seen as the biggest variable, with past US base returns in Korea taking about a decade. Reuters reported on 9 Oct that SK Hynix, a South Korean memory-chip maker, and Samsung each plan about 400 trillion won (US$298 billion) of investment in the Gwangju cluster, and no construction start date has been given.
notes: The pool item (Digitimes, subscription-only) was replaced by THE ELEC (11 Oct 2026), which carries the same military-base angle, and Reuters of 9 Oct 2026 for the plan's size; the url is THE ELEC. Event date 9 Oct 2026 and pool follow_up flag false, so the QA re-dated check may hold it; the Reuters visit story was pool only on 9 Oct, not in a report edition. Digitimes headline figure US$299 billion matches Reuters' 400 trillion won.
